dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: pṛṣṭhaśūnyaṃ mūlaśūnyaṃ hṛcchūnyam bhāvayet sthiram | yugapan nirvikalpatvān nirvikalpodayas tataḥ ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
sanskrit_variants: verse 45: GRETIL reads pṛṣṭa-; corrected to pṛṣṭha- with Wallis, Pradīpaka and Singh (legible as 'Pr~thasiinyam' in the scan).
dharana.rendering: Let one steadily contemplate, all at once, the void above, the void at the root and the void in the heart. Because this is free of thought-constructs all at once, the thought-free state arises.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh reports Śivopādhyāya's reading: the void above stands for the knowing subject (pramātṛ), the void at the root for the objects (prameya), and the void in the heart for knowing itself (pramāṇa), each contemplated as void. Wallis: the space above, at the root, and in the heart, simultaneously.
dharana.technique_name: Three Voids at Once: Above, Base and Heart
dharana.instruction: Feel open space above the head, in the heart and at the base, all at once.

verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 45 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: void above (commentarial: at or above the crown)
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is three open spaces on the vertical line (above, heart, base) held at the same moment and steadily.
geometry.svg_hint: a vertical line with three open circles (above the head, at the chest, at the base) all highlighted together
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Three spaces, one stillness
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: three open spaces held together leave no room for the next thought. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Hold all three spaces steadily and together
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The voids above, in the heart and at the base, held at once and steadily

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Let one steadily contemplate, all at once, the void above, the void at the root and the void in the heart. Because this is free of thought-constructs all at once, the thought-free state arises.
adiyogi.method_summary: Feel an open space above the head, in the heart and at the base of the trunk, all three together, and hold that steadily without moving between them. Let the thought-free state come by itself.

honesty.disclosure: Door 022 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 22 (verse 45) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 022 is dharana 22, verse 45. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. If holding three places feels effortful, return to two (Door 021) or one. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

beats.script: This is Door 022: three voids at once. Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 22, verse 45.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make. Any easy seat. The map is three open spaces on the body's line: above, heart, base.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Let the floor or the chair carry you. Eyes closed or soft.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps. No forced hold.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Feel all three spaces together and steadily. Do not move between them. Let them stay open at once.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: three open spaces leave no room for the next thought. A metaphor, not medicine.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 45: steadily contemplate the void above, the void at the base and the void in the heart at once; the thought-free state arises.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Let the breath go unwatched for a round. Move the fingers and toes. Return to the room.
